appliesTo: any person making electioneering communications that portray a candidate or elected official subject to recall via AI-created, altered, or digitally manipulated content

dutySources.disclosure-ui: § 1463(F)(1) — 'without providing a clear and understandable disclosure on the electioneering communication that it was created using artificial intelligence'

sources.prohibition: § 1463(F)(1) — 'No person shall make or cause to be made any electioneering communication that portrays a candidate or an elected official subject to recall and that is, through the use of artificial intelligence, created, altered, or digitally manipulated'
sources.penaltyMax: § 1463(G) — 'shall be fined not more than two thousand dollars or be imprisoned, with or without hard labor, for not more than two years, or both'
sources.penaltyUnit: § 1463(G) — 'Whoever violates any provision of this Section'

flags: criminal penalty includes imprisonment 'with or without hard labor, for not more than two years' — exposure vocabulary has no imprisonment field

penalty attaches only to violations 'with the intent to injure the reputation of a candidate or elected official subject to recall or to otherwise deceive a voter'; the underlying prohibition in (F)(1) states no intent element

functions as a disclosure regime (AI depiction permitted with disclosure) and dataset files it under Elections, but election-disclosure family is designated civil; coded ai-crimes because the only enforcement stated is criminal
depicted subjects are candidates and elected officials subject to recall — ai-crimes coveredSubjects enum (minors|all-persons) does not fit, so param omitted
§ 1463(I) exempts a 'media entity' broadcasting a paid communication in which 'the broadcaster has had no input in or control over' the content
required disclosure form cross-references 'the disclosure requirements of Subsection (E) of this Section' — not coded per no-imports rule

bill also amends non-AI campaign-finance provisions: definitions of contribution/coordinated expenditure/electioneering communication (§ 1483) and reporting by persons other than candidates or committees for expenditures exceeding 'one thousand dollars in the aggregate' (§ 1501.1(A)(1))
